one_liner: ARM's NEON-optimized C library whose FFTs (float, Q31, Q15) beat FFmpeg's assembly FFT on an Android phone.
what_it_does: Ne10 is a C library of NEON-optimized math, DSP, image-processing and physics routines for ARMv7 and AArch64 (Linux, Android, iOS); the FFT part covers 1-D complex-to-complex and real-to-complex/complex-to-real transforms in FP32, Q31 and Q15. The API is KissFFT-like: allocate a size-specific configuration with ne10_fft_alloc_c2c_float32(n), call ne10_fft_c2c_1d_float32(out, in, cfg, inverse) out of place, then destroy the config. Generic entry points are function pointers that ne10_init() binds to the NEON or plain-C variant at run time; the _c and _neon variants can also be called directly.
how_it_is_fast: It runs a mixed-radix Cooley-Tukey FFT (radix 2/3/4/5, with a combined radix-8 first stage) over twiddle and factor tables precomputed in the config. For sizes divisible by 4 the NEON path splits the transform into four interleaved sub-FFTs processed across NEON lanes, then finishes with a 'super twiddle' last stage. Power-of-two kernels exist as NEON intrinsics and, on ARMv7 builds, as hand-written NEON assembly (*.neon.s); the issue #165 figure is for that '(asm)' path.
when_to_use: 32-bit ARMv7-A Android or Linux targets with NEON where you need a small, permissively licensed FFT; the hand-written assembly path is enabled only on ARMv7.
Audio and DSP on phones and embedded Cortex-A: power-of-two complex or real FFTs (e.g. 256-4096 points) reusing one config per size.
Fixed-point pipelines that need Q15 or Q31 FFTs with optional per-stage scaling (scaled_flag), which most float-only libraries lack.
Projects that already use other Ne10 DSP blocks (FIR, IIR) and want one consistent ARM library.
when_not_to_use: x86 or any non-ARM target: CMake refuses non-ARM Linux builds, and there is no SSE/AVX code.
Double precision, multi-dimensional or batched transforms: not provided (issues #243, #234 and #251 ask for doubles and 2-D).
Arbitrary lengths: float C2C needs 2^a*3^b*5^c (NEON also needs N % 4 == 0 above 2), and the int32, int16 and real transforms are powers of two only; alloc returns NULL otherwise.

If you need the fastest NEON FFT: the only head-to-head (issue #165) has SuperpoweredFFT about 1.37x faster than Ne10 at N=1024 (derived from page data), and there is no comparison against FFTW, KissFFT or PFFFT on the repo pages read here.

Toolchain-sensitive builds: reports of all-zero output with NDK r20 clang (#237), broken r2c/c2r at N >= 4096 under -Ofast (#241) and AArch64 NDK/iOS build failures (#239, #252), with no maintainer fixes since 2018.

integration.min_toolchain: CMake; GCC with GNU assembler syntax (C built as gnu99, some FFT files are C++); Android NDK with API level >= 21 and GCC >= 4.8 for AArch64; iOS 7.0+
integration.platforms: ARMv7-A with NEON and AArch64 on Linux, Android and iOS; math and physics modules are ARMv7-only; no non-ARM support
integration.thread_safety: One config per thread: each cfg holds a scratch buffer used during the transform, and issue #218 (open, unanswered) reports that sharing a plan across threads fails.

gotchas: Call ne10_init() before using the generic names (ne10_fft_c2c_1d_float32 and so on); they are function pointers that ne10_init() binds to the NEON or C variant.
Scaling: by default only the inverse transform is scaled by 1/N; the fixed-point variants take a scaled_flag; sizes below 15 silently fall back to the C path.

The root CMakeLists.txt aborts unless CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR starts with 'arm', so native builds on hosts that report 'aarch64' hit that check; the GAS-syntax assembly is also awkward for clang outside the iOS toolchain file.
NEON and C fixed-point Q31 results differ slightly (#233), and the R2C example comment in NE10_dsp.h is reported wrong (#267).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Ne10 over SYLT-FFT when the target is a NEON-capable Cortex-A rather than a Cortex-M4. Pick it over PFFFT or PocketFFT when you need Q15/Q31 fixed-point FFTs or ARMv7 hand-tuned assembly; prefer those for portable or x86 code or maintained sources.
verified_claims_summary: A single third-party post (issue #165, 2017) reports cycles for a 1024-point complex FFT on a Samsung Galaxy S6: Ne10 (asm) 10125 vs FFmpeg libavcodec (asm) 14375, about 1.42x faster (derived from page data), also ahead of tricl_fft and CkFft but behind SuperpoweredFFT (7375). The post gives no compiler, flags, Ne10 version, timing method or code, and does not define 'cycles'.
status_note: Abandoned since 2018-11-15 (no releases or maintainer replies to the FFT bug reports read here, about 100 open issues) but BSD-3-Clause (ARM Limited), 1.5k stars and small enough to vendor; pin your toolchain and test outputs.
